Front Range spacecraft builders and the Commerce City refinery: who certifies Denver NDT staff to NAS 410, and who to SNT-TC-1A

Aerospace NDT around Denver is mostly space hardware. Lockheed Martin's space business centers on its Waterton Canyon campus southwest of the city and reports more than 14,000 Colorado employees. BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems, the former Ball Aerospace, works across Boulder, Broomfield and Westminster. Sierra Space is based in Louisville, launch-vehicle and satellite companies cluster in Centennial and Littleton, and Buckley Space Force Base sits in Aurora. The metro's other inspection economy is Suncor's Commerce City refinery, Colorado's only refinery, with the DJ Basin's gathering systems and gas plants to the north. The two economies certify people under different documents, and a technician can hold a valid certification on one side and none on the other.

Front Range employers and the standard each usually uses

Who you work forPersonnel standard you are likely to meetWhy
A spacecraft or launch-vehicle prime's own inspection groupThe company's own written practice; ask which standard and revision it followsPrimes run their own programs and audit their suppliers against them
A machine, weld, composite or finishing shop selling to those primesCommonly NAS 410, named in the purchase orderQuality clauses flow down to each sub-tier that inspects flight hardware
A Nadcap-accredited processorNAS 410 run by a designated Responsible Level 3AC7114 auditors trace every certification to training, experience, examination and vision records
Suncor Commerce City or a refinery inspection contractorSNT-TC-1A, with API 510, 570 and 653 inspection programs above itASME Section V and the API codes, adopted through the written practice
A DJ Basin, pipeline or structural steel contractorSNT-TC-1AAPI 1104, the ASME B31 codes and AWS D1.1

Crossing from Commerce City to a space supplier

A refinery UT technician who takes a job at a Broomfield or Littleton supplier is certified again under the new employer's program. The shop's RL3 reviews course outlines and hours, the signed experience log, past examinations and the vision record, credits what the written practice allows, and sets the rest. Three things usually change. Penetrant and eddy current displace thickness gauging as the daily methods. NAS 410 expects more formal, documented penetrant and magnetic particle training than SNT-TC-1A recommends, so that is where the gap tends to be. And the specific examination tests the prime's procedures and acceptance criteria, not a refinery code. An SNT-TC-1A certificate helps the review along, but it does not by itself meet a NAS 410 requirement.

For Front Range suppliers carrying both kinds of order

Some Denver-area shops machine flight brackets one week and repair refinery valves the next. Keep separate written practices or clearly separate sections, print the standard and revision on every certification, keep training records to the NAS 410 standard of evidence from the start, and apply the stricter vision and examination rule wherever the two documents differ. Agree with your customers when to move NAS 410 work to Revision 6, released in December 2025. Level III audit support for aerospace and NAS 410 audit documentation support cover the preparation and review your RL3 then approves.

Atlantis on the Front Range

Atlantis training is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A: self-paced online theory with Q&A from our ASNT NDT Level III (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT), rehearsal in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on practical at your employer's facility. There is no Atlantis classroom in Denver. Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3 to Front Range space or refinery employers. A space supplier's RL3 decides whether outside coursework counts toward that company's NAS 410 certifications, so ask before enrolling. Read NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A and the aerospace NDT certification requirements; method pages include penetrant testing training and ultrasonic testing training. Readers south of the Palmer Divide can see NDT training in Colorado Springs.
